concepts.statement: Recognising a described product or task as a computer-vision workload: the input is images or video and the required answer must be read out of pixels — what is present, where it is, or what text appears in a scene

Recognising a described product or task as a natural language processing workload: the material being interpreted or produced is human language — text or utterances — and the value comes from understanding what it says

Recognising a document-processing workload and telling it apart from generic text reading: the goal is structured fields captured out of forms, receipts or contracts — not merely the characters on the page
Recognising a generative-AI workload by what happens to content: new text, images or code are created on request, rather than existing content being classified, scored or extracted
Discriminating between the four AI workload categories when a scenario carries surface features of more than one — the deciding question is what the output must be, not what the input looks like
Fairness as equitable treatment of similarly situated people — reading a measured outcome disparity as a fairness failure, and naming fairness when another responsible-AI principle plausibly applies
Reliability and safety as a design consideration: the system must behave consistently and safely under both expected and unexpected conditions, and the design work is anticipating the unexpected ones
Privacy and security as a responsible-AI principle: protecting the personal data an AI system learns from and handles, and securing the system itself — two obligations under one principle
Inclusiveness as engaging and empowering everyone the system serves, including people with disabilities — a design consideration about who can benefit, not only a definition to recall

The transparency-versus-accountability boundary: transparency makes how and why a decision was made intelligible to the people it affects, accountability keeps humans answerable for the system — explaining is not the same duty as owning
Choosing the action that discharges a named responsible-AI principle — every option is something a competent team might do, and only one of them answers the principle actually named
Recognising a regression scenario by its output shape: the model must predict a continuous numeric quantity, and that requirement — not the subject matter — is what selects the technique
Recognising a classification scenario by its output shape: the model assigns each case to a category, with binary and multiclass as the two forms of the same technique

Recognising a clustering scenario by the absence of predefined labels and the goal of discovering groupings — with supervision as the dividing line across all three techniques: regression and classification learn from labelled data, clustering does not

What makes a technique deep learning: layered neural networks that learn their own representations of the data, chosen when features are too complex to hand-describe — a technique decision, not a buzzword
What the Transformer architecture contributes — attention over whole sequences rather than word-by-word processing — and why modern language models are built on it

Telling a feature from a label in a described dataset: the features are the columns the model is given, the label is the column it must learn to predict — and only supervised techniques need the label at all
vocabulary: features and labels in a dataset

concepts.statement: Why data is split into training and validation sets, and how to read a large train-versus-validation performance gap as a generalisation failure — the model memorised its training data instead of learning from it

Matching an Azure Machine Learning capability to the people who will use it: automated machine learning runs the multi-algorithm search for teams without data-science depth, the designer gives a visual pipeline surface, notebooks and the SDK serve code-first practitioners

Separating compute resources from training capabilities in Azure Machine Learning: compute is where work runs, training capabilities are what the work does — a scenario that needs more of one is not asking for the other
vocabulary: data and compute services for data science and machine learning

concepts.statement: Registering, versioning and managing trained models as first-class assets: knowing which model version is deployed, and being able to roll back to a previous one, is a capability a team must plan for — not a by-product of training
vocabulary: model management capabilities in Azure Machine Learning

concepts.statement: Choosing how a trained model is served from the consuming application's needs: per-request answers with low latency select a real-time endpoint, periodic scoring of accumulated data selects batch
vocabulary: deployment capabilities in Azure Machine Learning

concepts.statement: Image classification assigns one label to the whole image — the right choice exactly when the scenario needs a per-image verdict and nothing about where things are inside it
Object detection returns a class and a location for each instance found — selected when the scenario needs to know what is in the image and where or how many, per object
Optical character recognition extracts text that already exists in an image — reading what is written, as opposed to describing what is pictured or generating anything new
vocabulary: features of optical character recognition solutions

concepts.statement: Facial detection locates faces in an image and facial analysis describes their attributes — age estimation, head pose, occlusion — two capabilities that operate on faces without saying whose face it is
vocabulary: features of facial detection and facial analysis solutions

concepts.statement: The boundary between facial analysis and identifying a person: detection and attribute estimation answer 'is there a face and what is it like', identification claims 'this is who' — a different capability with materially heavier responsible-AI weight
vocabulary: facial detection and facial analysis solutions

concepts.statement: Choosing between the computer-vision solution types by the granularity of the required output — a whole-image label, per-instance classes and locations, or extracted text — never by the subject matter pictured

Azure AI Vision's descriptive analysis features — captioning an image in natural language, tagging its contents, smart-cropping around what matters — and telling those features of one service apart when a requirement names only what the output should be
vocabulary: capabilities of the Azure AI Vision service

concepts.statement: Azure AI Vision's Read capability delivers OCR as a service feature — extracting printed and handwritten text from images — and is a different feature of the same service than describing or tagging the scene
vocabulary: capabilities of the Azure AI Vision service

concepts.statement: What Azure AI Face does — face detection, attribute analysis and face-specific processing — and where the boundary sits between it and Azure AI Vision's people detection: knowing people are present is Vision's job, working with faces as faces is Face's
vocabulary: capabilities of the Azure AI Face detection service

concepts.statement: Matching a described vision requirement to the right one of the two blueprint-named vision services — Azure AI Vision or Azure AI Face — by what the requirement needs done, with off-list services as recognisable wrong turns
vocabulary: Azure tools and services for computer vision tasks

concepts.statement: The limit of OCR in a vision pipeline: reading text yields characters and their positions, while structured fields out of a form — names, totals, dates bound to their meaning — is document processing, a requirement pure text extraction cannot meet

Key phrase extraction surfaces the main talking points of a text without assigning them types — the right feature when the requirement is 'what is this text about', not 'which entities does it mention'
Entity recognition finds and categorises typed items in text — person, place, organisation, quantity, date — selected when the requirement needs values bound to types, not just the words that matter
Sentiment analysis scores opinion polarity over a document or sentence — the feature a scenario needs when the question is how people feel about something, not what they said about it
Language modelling maps an utterance to an intent and pulls out its entities — the capability behind systems that must decide what a user wants done from how they phrased it
Speech recognition and speech synthesis as the two directions of one capability — audio into text, text into audio — and recognising when a scenario needs one direction, the other, or both
Translation between languages as a capability that exists for both text and speech — with the delivery differing by medium, so the scenario's medium decides where the capability comes from

Choosing between key phrase extraction, entity recognition and sentiment analysis when a scenario says only 'extract information from text' — the discrimination that separates knowing feature names from reading a requirement
Azure AI Language's text-analytics coverage: sentiment, key phrases, entity recognition and language detection live in one service — a scenario needing several of them needs one service, not several
vocabulary: capabilities of the Azure AI Language service

concepts.statement: Azure AI Language's conversational features — conversational language understanding classifies intent, custom question answering retrieves answers — as the current successors to the retired LUIS and QnA Maker brands, and the classify-versus-retrieve line between them
vocabulary: capabilities of the Azure AI Language service

concepts.statement: What Azure AI Speech covers — speech-to-text, text-to-speech, and speech translation — so a requirement that lives in audio, in either direction or across languages, resolves to this one service
vocabulary: capabilities of the Azure AI Speech service

concepts.statement: Matching a described language requirement to Azure AI Language or Azure AI Speech by where the content lives: written text belongs to Language, spoken audio to Speech — the medium decides, not the task's vocabulary
vocabulary: Azure tools and services for NLP workloads

concepts.statement: What makes a model generative: it produces new content — text, images, code — in response to input, where a predictive model returns a label or a score about content that already exists

Recognising which generative model family a requirement needs — a language model, an image-generation model, an embedding model or a speech model — from what the output must be, not from which family is most famous

The common generative-AI scenario shapes — natural-language generation, summarisation, code generation, image generation, conversational assistance — and recognising which shape a described product is

Hallucination as generative AI's headline limitation — fluent, plausible output that is not grounded in anything true — and grounding the model in real content as the response that addresses the mechanism rather than the symptom
vocabulary: responsible AI considerations for generative AI

concepts.statement: Platform-level content filtering as the built-in safety layer of a generative service: harmful input and output categories are caught by the platform before an application ever sees them — protection an application inherits rather than writes
vocabulary: responsible AI considerations for generative AI

concepts.statement: Mitigating generative-AI failures in layers: platform filtering plus application-level instruction plus grounding stack together, so the right response to a bad output adds or strengthens a layer — removing one is never the fix
vocabulary: responsible AI considerations for generative AI

concepts.statement: Transparency obligations specific to generated content: people interacting with an AI assistant or consuming AI-made material should be able to know that is what it is — disclosure is part of deploying generative AI responsibly
vocabulary: responsible AI considerations for generative AI

concepts.statement: What Azure AI Foundry is: the portal and platform where generative AI solutions are built, tested and deployed — the place a team works, as distinct from any single model it works with (rebranded Microsoft Foundry in current documentation)
vocabulary: features and capabilities of Azure AI Foundry

concepts.statement: What Azure OpenAI Service provides — access to OpenAI's model families with Azure's enterprise controls — and where it sits relative to Azure AI Foundry: one model provider reachable through the broader platform
vocabulary: features and capabilities of Azure OpenAI service

concepts.statement: What the Azure AI Foundry model catalog is for: browsing, comparing and deploying models from multiple providers — the capability a scenario needs when the requirement is choosing among models rather than calling a known one
vocabulary: features and capabilities of Azure AI Foundry model catalog

concepts.statement: Choosing between building a solution in Azure AI Foundry and calling a model directly, from what the scenario needs: orchestration, testing and deployment surface versus a single model answering requests
vocabulary: generative AI services and capabilities in Microsoft Azure

concepts.statement: Where persistent behavioural constraints belong: a system message shapes every response for the assistant's lifetime, while per-request examples shape only the request that carries them — a persistent rule placed per-prompt is placed wrong
vocabulary: generative AI services and capabilities in Microsoft Azure

concepts.statement: Grounding generated answers in an organisation's own content: retrieval feeds the model the relevant documents at question time — the technique for answering from a private corpus, where fine-tuning or a bigger context window answer different problems
vocabulary: generative AI services and capabilities in Microsoft Azure
